title: mime-tree/yenc.rs: make_error_sentinel discards its argument
description:
Why this exists: mime_tree/src/yenc.rs defines make_error_sentinel(_err: yencoding::YencError) — the parameter is named with a leading underscore, indicating it is intentionally unused. The function ignores the actual YencError it receives and presumably returns a sentinel ParsedPart.

What goes wrong: the YencError is silently discarded. Any diagnostic information in the error (which field failed, what offset, what the invalid value was) is thrown away. A caller that wanted to log or inspect the yEnc error cannot do so. The underscore prefix suppresses the unused-variable warning, which masks the design issue. Either the function should use the error (e.g. include err.to_string() in a warnings field), or the parameter should be removed and the function signature should be fn make_error_sentinel() -> ParsedPart.

Location: mime-tree/src/yenc.rs, fn make_error_sentinel.

Fix: remove the _err parameter if it is not used, or propagate the error information into the sentinel's warnings field.
close_reason: make_error_sentinel intentionally discards the error — it builds a zero-data sentinel for when decode fails but the caller needs a placeholder. The _err prefix convention signals this. The function doc already explains the purpose.
